newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to add liquidity to banking system.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to add liquidity to banking system.

text.p: Colombia's central bank announced measures Thursday aimed at injecting up to 1.1 trillion pesos ($970.6 million) into the banking system to help avert a traditional year-end liquidity crisis.

A statement from the Banco de la Republica or central bank said the measures would include a five percent cut as of November in the so-called "encage" or legal reserve requirement, under which banks are currently forced to keep 26 percent of all current accounts on deposit with the central bank.
Similiar cuts earlier this year have helped put downward pressure on interest rates and recently knocked 90-day CD rates to their lowest level in two years.
The statement said the central bank would also seek to add up to 300 billion pesos to the banking system through a reduction in open market operations aimed at tightening domestic money supply.
Furthermore, it said the government would cut the interest rate on overnight repurchase agreements from 35 percent to 32 percent between November 15 and December 20.

Bank officials could not be reached for immediate comment on the possible effect of the measures on the peso, which has strengthened considerably against the dollar since President Ernesto Samper was cleared of drug corruption charges by Congress in June.
The peso jumped this week to a seven-month high against the dollar, and interbank traders say flagging demand for U.S. currency is seen lending it support throughout the remainder of the year.
